editorial: You follow Zain, a tough 12-year-old boy living in poverty in Lebanon. After running away from his careless parents, he ends up on the streets taking care of a baby named Yonas. The movie shows his hard life through his eyes, and you feel every moment of his struggle. The story is raw and real, pulling you into a world most people never see. The acting is incredible, especially from the young lead who feels completely natural. The pacing keeps you engaged even during quiet moments. The downside is that it can be emotionally heavy and hard to watch at times. If you enjoy powerful dramas that stay with you, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Zain is in court suing his parents for bringing him into a life of suffering. He finally gets his photo taken for an ID card, something he never had before. The twist is that this small moment gives him an identity and a sense of hope. The movie ends with him smiling for the camera, showing that even after everything he went through, there is still a chance for a better future ahead.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful real-life stories and character-driven dramas.
